caption: The drawing depicts a single object, which is a sculpted candlestick holder designed in the shape of a fish. The fish is upright, with its mouth open and facing upward, forming the base of the candle holder. The fish has a detailed, textured body with visible scales, fins, and a curling, upward-pointing tail, all rendered in shades of bluish-gray with subtle highlights and shadows to give a metallic appearance. The fish stands on a rectangular base, also shaded in bluish-gray tones. The candlestick holder portion emerges from the fish's open mouth, featuring a fluted design with a petal-like rim, consistent in color and texture with the rest of the object. The background is plain and off-white, with no additional objects or decorations, and there is a small area in the lower right corner where the name "John Hall" is written in uppercase letters.
title: Glass Candlestick
cluster: #19 — Ceramic Arts: Pottery, Stoneware, and Porcelain
